summary: The animate-expo RECIPES file gives ready-to-build React Native and Expo implementations for the motion that comes up most: press feedback, a drag-to-dismiss bottom sheet, swipe to delete, a collapsing header, list entrances, keyboard-synced UI, a tab indicator, native screen transitions, toasts and firing something once at a threshold. Each recipe states the exact values (durations, springs, curves, offsets, interpolation ranges) and the few details that separate a fluid version from a broken one, such as capturing the current value on grab, deciding by projected velocity, handing velocity to the spring and clamping interpolation. It also shares two worklets, Apple-style momentum projection and rubber-banding. For a design system it supplies concrete mobile motion tokens and component behaviors that can be locked as defaults, plus platform differences for native sheets on iOS and Android.
key_ideas: Check for a native component first (formSheet, ReanimatedSwipeable, native stack) and hand-build only when the interaction is different in kind.
Momentum projection decides where a flick was going, so a fast short swipe commits and a slow long one doesn't.
Rubber-banding makes a boundary resist instead of stopping dead.
Grabbing an element mid-animation must continue from where it is on screen, not jump back to zero.
Handing the release velocity to the spring removes the seam between finger and animation.
Derive related visuals (a backdrop, a header title) from the same shared value so they stay in sync for free.
Collapse headers by translating content in a fixed-height, clipped container, never by animating height.
Never put entrance animations on rows of a virtualized list; recycled rows re-fire and flicker.
Drive keyboard-following UI from the keyboard's real position, not from an event plus a guessed duration.
Toasts stay under 300ms, exit the way they entered, exit about 20% faster, and respect safe-area insets.
Fire one-off effects at a threshold with useAnimatedReaction, so the JS call happens only when the state flips.
Build gestures and layout-animation builders once (useMemo or module scope), not on every render.

rules.rule: Install react-native-reanimated, react-native-worklets, react-native-gesture-handler and expo-haptics with npx expo install, not npm install; add react-native-keyboard-controller only when keyboard-synced UI is needed.
rules.why: expo install resolves the versions that match the SDK.
values: npx expo install react-native-reanimated react-native-worklets react-native-gesture-handler expo-haptics

rules.rule: Wrap the app once in GestureHandlerRootView with style { flex: 1 }; in Expo Router, do it in the root _layout.
rules.why: Setup every gesture recipe assumes.

rules.rule: Define the shared easing constants once: EASE_OUT = Easing.bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1) for UI, EASE_IN_OUT = Easing.bezier(0.77, 0, 0.175, 1) for on-screen movement, EASE_SHEET = Easing.bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1) for the iOS sheet curve.
rules.why: The recipes share these constants, commented as the strong ease-out for UI, on-screen movement and the iOS sheet curve.
rules.evidence: Imports and constants every recipe below shares

rules.rule: Read and write shared values with .get() / .set() rather than .value.
rules.why: It is the form the Reanimated docs recommend for React Compiler support; .value still works, but the compiler can't see through it.

rules.rule: Call back to the React Native runtime from a worklet with scheduleOnRN(fn, ...args), not the deprecated runOnJS(fn)(...args).
rules.why: scheduleOnRN replaces runOnJS.

rules.rule: Wrap Gesture Handler v2 gestures in useMemo.
rules.why: Rebuilding a gesture on every render can reattach the recognizer and drop a drag that's mid-flight.
rules.evidence: Rebuilding a gesture on every render can reattach the recognizer

rules.rule: On Gesture Handler v3, use the hook form (e.g. usePanGesture with one config object), map onStart to onActivate and onEnd to onDeactivate, read the inverted event.canceled instead of success, and drop the useMemo.
rules.why: In v3 the builder is legacy and the hook manages its own identity.

rules.rule: Decide where a flick was going with momentum projection: project(velocity, decelerationRate = 0.998) = ((velocity / 1000) * decelerationRate) / (1 - decelerationRate).
rules.why: A fast short swipe should commit and a slow long one shouldn't; this is Apple's exponential-decay form, not v²/2a.

rules.rule: Make boundaries resist with rubberband(overshoot, dimension, constant = 0.55) = (overshoot * dimension * constant) / (dimension + constant * Math.abs(overshoot)).
rules.why: The further past the edge, the less the element follows, instead of stopping dead.

rules.rule: Give every pressable a press scale of 0.97 over 120ms with transitionTimingFunction cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1) on transform, and treat 120ms and a 3% scale as the ceiling for something touched this often.
rules.why: It passes the frequency gate only because it's near-imperceptible; anything longer or larger belongs to rarer moments.
rules.evidence: a CSS transition is the whole implementation

rules.rule: Implement press feedback as a CSS transition on an Animated.View toggled by onPressIn / onPressOut, with no gesture and no shared value.
rules.why: A CSS transition is the whole implementation; setState is fine because it fires twice per press, not per frame.

rules.rule: Use hitSlop (the recipe sets hitSlop={12}) to bring a small icon up to the 44pt target without growing it, and pressRetentionOffset (the recipe sets pressRetentionOffset={16}) so slight finger drift doesn't cancel the press.
rules.why: hitSlop brings a small icon up to the 44pt target without growing it; pressRetentionOffset stops a slight finger drift from cancelling.

rules.rule: If a bottom sheet is its own destination, use presentation: 'formSheet'; build a custom drag-to-dismiss sheet only when it has to live inside an existing screen.
rules.why: formSheet gives the platform's real sheet for free.
rules.evidence: Bottom sheet you can drag to dismiss

rules.rule: Give a vertical sheet pan activeOffsetY([-10, 10]).
rules.why: Lets a horizontal swipe win and requires intent before committing.
rules.evidence: Bottom sheet you can drag to dismiss

rules.rule: In a drag gesture's onStart, capture the current on-screen value (context.set(translateY.get())) and add the translation to it.
rules.why: Without it, grabbing a sheet mid-animation teleports it; the animation must continue from where the eye last saw it.
rules.evidence: start from the current on-screen value, not from 0

rules.rule: Let a sheet move freely downward and apply rubberband resistance when dragged upward past the top.
rules.why: Downward is free; upward past the top resists.
rules.evidence: downward is free; upward past the top resists

rules.rule: Decide sheet dismissal from the projected position (current position + project(velocityY)) against 40% of the sheet height, so a quick flick dismisses even a few pixels down.
rules.why: Velocity decides, not distance; requiring 40% travel makes the sheet feel heavy.

rules.rule: Dismiss a sheet with withSpring(HEIGHT, { duration: 300, dampingRatio: 1, velocity: e.velocityY, overshootClamping: true }) and call onClose via scheduleOnRN only when the spring finishes.
rules.why: Recipe values; overshootClamping stops the sheet springing past the bottom and flashing a gap.
values: duration: 300, dampingRatio: 1, velocity: e.velocityY, overshootClamping: true
rules.evidence: duration: 300, dampingRatio: 1, velocity: e.velocityY, overshootClamping: true

rules.rule: Snap a sheet back with withSpring(0, { duration: 300, dampingRatio: 0.8, velocity: e.velocityY }) and fire Haptics.impactAsync(Light) because it snapped home.
rules.why: Recipe values; the code comment marks the Light haptic as 'it snapped home'.

rules.rule: Hand the gesture's release velocity to the spring.
rules.why: There's no seam between the finger releasing and the animation continuing; this is the single detail that most separates fluid from fine.
rules.evidence: Velocity is handed to the spring

rules.rule: Use overshootClamping on sheet dismissal.
rules.why: Otherwise the sheet springs past the bottom of the screen and flashes a gap.
rules.evidence: otherwise the sheet springs past the bottom of the screen and flashes a gap

rules.rule: Derive the sheet backdrop's opacity from the sheet's own shared value: interpolate(translateY, [0, HEIGHT], [1, 0], Extrapolation.CLAMP).
rules.why: It's always in sync and costs nothing.
rules.evidence: The backdrop derives from the same value

rules.rule: Use ReanimatedSwipeable for rows that reveal action buttons; build the gesture yourself only for an interaction different in kind, such as swipe-to-commit with momentum projection.
rules.why: ReanimatedSwipeable already does thresholds, overshoot and open/close methods on the UI thread.

rules.rule: Declare the axis on any pan inside a scroll view, e.g. activeOffsetX([-10, 10]) for a horizontal row swipe.
rules.why: With no axis declared it steals vertical scrolls, and the list feels broken in a way that looks like a scrolling bug.
rules.evidence: A pan handler inside a scroll view with no axis declared will steal vertical scrolls

rules.rule: Commit a swipe-to-delete when the projected position passes -SWIPE_THRESHOLD: slide out with withTiming(-WIDTH, { duration: 200, easing: EASE_OUT }) and call onDelete when it finishes; otherwise spring back with { duration: 300, dampingRatio: 1, velocity: e.velocityX }.
rules.why: Recipe values: a committed swipe slides off with a 200ms ease-out timing and onDelete runs only when it finishes; an uncommitted one springs home with the release velocity.

rules.rule: Let the list close the gap a deleted row leaves, with itemLayoutAnimation={LinearTransition.duration(200)} defined at module scope.
rules.why: Closing the gap is the list's job, not the row's; builders rebuilt in render cost every re-render.
rules.evidence: Closing the gap the deleted row left is the list's job

rules.rule: Drive a collapsing header from useAnimatedScrollHandler into a shared value, fading title opacity 1 to 0 and moving translateY 0 to -12 over scroll 0 to 60, with scrollEventThrottle={16}.
rules.why: Recipe values.

rules.rule: Never animate a header's height to collapse it; give the container a fixed height, translate the content inside and clip with overflow: 'hidden'.
rules.why: Animating height runs a layout pass on the header and everything below it every scroll frame, competing with the scroll itself.
rules.evidence: Never animate the header's height to collapse it.

rules.rule: Pass Extrapolation.CLAMP to scroll-driven interpolations such as the collapsing header's; the source calls it not optional.
rules.why: Without it, scrolling past 60 keeps driving opacity negative and the header reappears inverted at the bottom of a long list.

rules.rule: Build layout-animation builders outside components or in useMemo; for a per-index delay, memoize it inside the row.
rules.why: An inline chain in JSX rebuilds the builder on every render.

rules.rule: Stagger list entrances by 30–80ms per item (the recipe uses FadeInDown.duration(250).delay(index * 40)).
rules.why: Longer feels slow; shorter reads as simultaneous.

rules.rule: Never put entering on a row inside FlatList, FlashList or any virtualized list; animate the list container once on mount, or use itemLayoutAnimation for reflow only.
rules.why: Rows are recycled, so the animation re-fires every time one scrolls back into view and the list appears to flicker.
rules.evidence: Never put entering on a row inside FlatList

rules.rule: Use entrance animations only for content the user asked for and is waiting on; a list they scroll past all day should already be there.
rules.why: A list they scroll past all day should already be there.
rules.evidence: Entrance animations are for content the user asked for

rules.rule: For keyboard-synced UI, install react-native-keyboard-controller and put KeyboardProvider in the root _layout next to GestureHandlerRootView.
rules.why: The hooks do nothing without the provider.

rules.rule: Move keyboard-following UI with useReanimatedKeyboardAnimation's height (0 to -keyboardHeight) applied as translateY on the UI thread.
rules.why: The UI must be driven by the keyboard's actual position, frame by frame.

rules.rule: Never build keyboard-following motion from Keyboard.addListener plus a timing animation.
rules.why: The keyboard rides a private system curve and the event arrives on the JS thread after it has started moving, so any duration visibly lags or leads it.

rules.rule: For a tab or segmented indicator, measure each tab once with onLayout (not per frame), then animate the pill's translateX and width with withTiming over 250ms using EASE_IN_OUT.
rules.why: Measure once, then animate transforms; ease-in-out because the pill is moving across the screen rather than entering or leaving it.

rules.rule: Animate the indicator pill's width rather than scaleX, since the pill is absolutely positioned with no children.
rules.why: Nothing else re-lays-out and the corner radius survives; scaleX would smear the corners into ovals.
rules.evidence: This is the sanctioned width animation

rules.rule: Fire Haptics.selectionAsync() when the tab is pressed, not when the pill lands.
rules.why: Stated as a directive with no separate reason in this file; it matches firing a haptic at the causal moment [inferred].
rules.evidence: on the press, not when the pill lands

rules.rule: Configure screen transitions on the native stack; never rebuild a screen transition in JS.
rules.why: The native one runs on the platform side, keeps the interactive back gesture and matches every other app on the device.

rules.rule: Use animation: 'default' (the unmodified platform push) when going deeper into a hierarchy.
rules.why: Navigation table: deeper into a hierarchy gets the platform push, unmodified.

rules.rule: Use presentation: 'modal' for a self-contained task the user can abandon.
rules.why: Navigation table.
rules.evidence: A self-contained task the user can abandon

rules.rule: Use presentation: 'formSheet' with detents for a short interruption such as a picker, filter or share.
rules.why: Navigation table.
rules.evidence: A short interruption: picker, filter, share

rules.rule: Use animation: 'none' between tabs.
rules.why: Navigation table.

rules.rule: Switch the stack's screenOptions to animation: 'fade' when reduced motion is on.
rules.why: Navigation table: reduced motion.

rules.rule: Set animationMatchesGesture: true whenever you set a custom animation on a screen.
rules.why: It makes the iOS back swipe run the transition in reverse under the finger; otherwise dragging back looks like a different app than pushing forward.
rules.evidence: animationMatchesGesture: true makes the iOS back swipe

rules.rule: Design form-sheet detents for at most three.
rules.why: Android caps detents at three; a longer sheetAllowedDetents array works on iOS and silently truncates on Android.

rules.rule: Don't rely on sheetGrabberVisible as the only 'this is draggable' affordance.
rules.why: It is iOS-only; Android shows no grabber.

rules.rule: Keep a form sheet's content a single screen; if it needs its own navigation, use presentation: 'modal' instead.
rules.why: Android form sheets can't host native headers or nested stacks.
rules.evidence: Android form sheets can't host native headers or nested stacks.

rules.rule: Give explicitly sized content to a sheet using sheetAllowedDetents: 'fitToContents'.
rules.why: A flex: 1 root has no intrinsic height to fit, so the detent is wrong.

rules.rule: Animate toasts in with FadeInDown.duration(300).easing(EASE_OUT) and out with FadeOutDown.duration(250).easing(EASE_OUT), with both builders at module scope.
rules.why: Recipe values; layout-animation builders live outside the component.

rules.rule: Keep toast animations within the 300ms cap.
rules.why: A toast is uninvited, so if anything it should be quicker and quieter than motion the user asked for.

rules.rule: Make a toast exit the way it entered.
rules.why: Entering from the bottom and leaving to the side reads as two unrelated elements.
rules.evidence: It exits the way it entered.

rules.rule: Make toast exits about 20% faster than entries.
rules.why: The user has finished reading; the arrival deserves the time, the departure doesn't.

rules.rule: Always offset toasts by the safe-area inset (e.g. bottom: insets.bottom + 16, left: 16, right: 16).
rules.why: A toast at bottom: 16 sits under the home indicator on every modern iPhone.

rules.rule: When stacked toasts reflow, add itemLayoutAnimation and tune the opacity against the reflow by eye, then look at it again the next day.
rules.why: There's no formula for that pair.
rules.evidence: If toasts stack and the list reflows

rules.rule: To fire something once when a crossing point is reached (a detent, a snap, pull-to-refresh arming), use useAnimatedReaction comparing on the UI thread and call JS only when the state flips; don't poll from JS and don't scheduleOnRN every frame.
rules.why: The comparison runs on the UI thread every frame; the JS call happens twice per pull.
rules.evidence: Firing something once at a threshold

rules.rule: Fire a Light impact haptic when a pull crosses its refresh threshold in either direction.
rules.why: Recipe: the reaction schedules Haptics.impactAsync(Light) when isArmed changes.
rules.evidence: Firing something once at a threshold

rules.rule: Start from the matching recipe, then adapt it to the case.
rules.why: The recipes are ready-to-build implementations for the cases that come up most in a React Native app.
rules.evidence: Start from the recipe, then adapt.

rules.rule: Let a swipe-to-delete row follow the finger only toward the delete side, clamping its position with Math.min(0, context.get() + e.translationX).
rules.why: Shown in the recipe's onUpdate; the source states no separate reason.

decisions.question: Should a bottom sheet be the platform's native sheet or a custom drag-to-dismiss sheet?

options.name: presentation: 'formSheet'
options.effect: The platform's real sheet for free, with detents; Android caps detents at three and shows no grabber.
options.when: The sheet is its own destination.

options.name: Custom drag-to-dismiss sheet
options.effect: A shared-value sheet with projection, rubber-banding, velocity-handed springs and a derived backdrop.
options.when: The sheet has to live inside an existing screen.

decisions.recommendation: formSheet whenever the sheet is its own destination; custom only when it must live inside a screen.
decisions.evidence: Bottom sheet you can drag to dismiss

options.name: ReanimatedSwipeable
options.effect: Swipe-to-reveal action buttons with thresholds, overshoot and open/close methods on the UI thread.

options.name: Custom pan gesture
options.effect: Swipe-to-commit with momentum projection and a slide-out.
options.when: The interaction is different in kind, such as swipe to delete.

options.effect: Rows glide to close gaps.

options.name: No entrance
options.effect: The list is already there.

options.name: Same path, exit about 20% faster

process.detail: npx expo install the animation, worklets, gesture and haptics packages; wrap the root _layout in GestureHandlerRootView (and KeyboardProvider if needed); define EASE_OUT, EASE_IN_OUT and EASE_SHEET.

process.step: Check for a native option first
process.detail: formSheet for sheets that are destinations, ReanimatedSwipeable for action rows, native stack options for screen transitions; build by hand only when the interaction differs in kind.
Memoize it, declare the axis with activeOffsetX/Y([-10, 10]), capture the current value in onStart, add translation in onUpdate, apply rubberband past edges.
Add project(velocity) to the current position and compare with the threshold, so velocity decides rather than distance.
Pass the release velocity into withSpring; clamp overshoot on dismissal; call JS (onClose, onDelete, haptics) via scheduleOnRN in the completion callback or onEnd.
Compute backdrop opacity, header title fades and similar from the same shared value with interpolate and Extrapolation.CLAMP.

Row slides left under the finger; a projected pass beyond the threshold slides it off in 200ms ease-out and deletes; the list closes the gap with LinearTransition.duration(200).
Title fades out and moves up 12 over the first 60 of scroll inside a fixed-height, clipped container.
Footer translates up by the keyboard's live height, frame by frame.
Pill slides and resizes to the measured tab over 250ms ease-in-out, keeping its round corners.
settings slides from right with animationMatchesGesture, compose opens as a modal, filter opens as a formSheet sized to its content with a grabber on iOS.
Enters with FadeInDown over 300ms and exits with FadeOutDown over 250ms, both ease-out, positioned 16 above the bottom safe-area inset and 16 from each side.
A light haptic fires once each time the pull crosses the refresh threshold.

caveats: Pinned to commit 85e8e23; APIs are version-specific (Reanimated 4, react-native-worklets, Gesture Handler v2 builder vs v3 hooks) and may change.
The form-sheet platform differences come from the Expo modal docs at the time of writing; the source points there for the full list.
HEIGHT, WIDTH, SWIPE_THRESHOLD and REFRESH_THRESHOLD are placeholders the recipes leave undefined; only the 40% sheet threshold is a stated value.
Tuning toast opacity against a stacking reflow is explicitly by eye; the source says there is no formula.
Code snippets are illustrative starting points ('start from the recipe, then adapt'), not complete components.
